findings.reason: the gate must name one live measurement, and as written a node can report the fixture's closure residual in place of the map-fidelity number and still satisfy the sentence.
findings.text: §4's done-when measures the map-fidelity clause "with the certificate exterior posed on the exact support (followup f-cfs-exterior-on-exact-support)" and then says "Until that fixture lands, the certificate's exterior closure residual (0.006 to 0.018 at 550 to 5,158 cells) is reported beside the map's own booking term", but that followup is `data-status="resolved"` (2026-10-12T07:28:03), so the clause as written offers two different measurements for one gate and leaves the worker to decide which is live

findings.reason: a bound within 11% of a measured term, with an unstated second term of the same order, either fails at the coarse rung or the goalpost moves at implementation time, and the plan should fix the rung set or the bound now (5,000 and 10,000 where the measured terms are 0.0044 and smaller, or a stated combined budget).
findings.text: the map-fidelity bound is 1e-2 relative sup at about 2,000, 5,000 and 10,000 cells, and the plan's own cited booking term is 0.0090 at 2,098 cells (resolution decision of 2026-10-10, §5 line 62 of this review's snapshot line 171), i.e. 90% of the bound before the exterior closure residual of 0.006 to 0.018 is added; the plan states no achieved closure residual after the resolved fixture and no margin, so the 2,000-cell row of the gate cannot be read as pass or fail from the plan's own evidence

findings.reason: the sentence itself states both arms, their sets and the measured orders (1.976 limited, 2.13 diverted), so the worker has the criterion even though the citation dangles; recording the ruling as a decision is the repair and changes no endpoint.
findings.text: §2's done-when sets the amplitude clause's acceptance under "the two-arm acceptance ruling of 2026-10-05 below", but no ruling of that name or date exists anywhere below; the 2026-10-05 entries in Decisions are field representation and receipts-out-of-git, and the only other text with the phrase is a followup describing arms landing later

findings.reason: the node cannot show its own guard fires, so the retirement's central claim (deleted, not kept beside the new solve) rests on an assertion no run can falsify; a declared control (a reinstated route or a restored module failing by test id) is what makes the deletion measurable.
findings.text: §6's retirement done-when is "the deletion lands with the acceptance table green at its head and no test weakened to admit it", which for a deletion node measures only that §5's gate still passes: a reinstated route, or a module left behind, passes it, and "no test weakened" has no instrument attached so it can never fail

findings.reason: those named modules are the ones already landed (current.book at 06cc5abe1, gs.apply at 599339edf, the map's operands at the same merge), so the prescription reads as a record of the landed state rather than an unreviewed guess, and striking it is editorial; a new section would be the case to hold to the endpoint-only rule.
findings.text: §2 through §5 each prescribe implementation rather than the endpoint: §2 names `topology.read` replacing `Topology.read` and `read_with_connectivity` in `topology.py` and the policy extended in `solve_request.py`, §4 states the formula and the replaced map in `forward_operator.py`, and §5 fixes Newton-GMRES on the map's own JVP, "applied at one call site served from a `lax.scan`, with one line search"
